name: genometools
desc: Versatile open source genome analysis software
why: Genome analysis toolkit with real bioinformatics depth, though it is a heavy specialist library.

brief.what_it_is: GenomeTools is a free, open source collection of bioinformatics tools for genome informatics, combined into a single binary named gt. It is built on a C library, libgenometools, which provides classes for efficient implementation of sequence and annotation processing software. The homepage lists bundled tools including LTRharvest, Tallymer, uniquesub, AnnotationSketch, LTRdigest, MetaGenomeThreader, GtEncseq and Readjoiner, plus tools built on the library such as GenomeThreader, ParsEval, LTRsift and FISH Oracle. The README does not spell out specific input and output formats beyond sequence and annotation data.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a versatile genome analysis system that bundles many published bioinformatics tools into one place rather than separate programs. The README frames it as a collection of tools that share a common library for efficient processing of sequence and annotation data.
brief.how_it_works: Tools are exposed as subcommands of one binary, gt, which sits on top of the C library libgenometools. The library's modules provide the shared data structures for sequences and structured genome annotations, and each published tool is built on those modules.

commands_seen.context: Debian/Ubuntu install of the most recent stable version, run as root, which provides the gt executable.
Installs the library and development headers. The README says this is not needed just to use the tools.
macOS install via Homebrew on supported macOS versions.
Builds from source on a typical 64-bit Linux system; the README says this should usually suffice.
Installs a source build into the gt subdirectory of the home directory; the same options as the original make run must be repeated. Without prefix it installs system-wide and needs root.

brief.install_notes: Packages exist for Debian, Ubuntu, Homebrew on macOS and the AUR (per README badges). Building from source needs the Cairo libraries and development headers for AnnotationSketch support; without them, build with cairo=no, which drops AnnotationSketch. On 32-bit systems add 32bit=yes. Source tarballs are on GitHub releases, and the INSTALL file in the repository has full build instructions. No accounts or runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: It is one binary bundling many separately published research tools from the same group, including a shared sequence data structure (GtEncseq) and a drawing library (AnnotationSketch). Its method papers are cited directly on the homepage, which makes it a reference collection as well as a toolkit.
brief.status: Unknown, leaning maintained. The GitHub README has a live build-status badge and package badges for Debian, Ubuntu, Homebrew and AUR. The homepage footer reads 'Copyright 2006-2023' but also says 'Last update: 2014-11-05', which is inconsistent. I did not find a release date or last commit date in the pages I read.
brief.caveats: The homepage says it is designed for POSIX systems such as Linux and macOS, with only a reduced Windows version available. Building from source can need Cairo headers, and skipping Cairo drops AnnotationSketch. The project is described as a heavy specialist library rather than a simple command-line utility. The homepage's 2014 last-update date conflicts with its 2023 copyright.
quotes: The GenomeTools genome analysis system is a free collection of bioinformatics tools (in the realm of genome informatics) combined into a single binary named gt.
GenomeTools has been designed to run on every POSIX compliant UNIX system, for example, Linux, macOS, and OpenBSD.
To report a bug, ask a question, or suggest new features, use the GenomeTools issue tracker.
